row.notes: In Game_SaveData_SerialiseContainer_2 (inline profile save), between storing the 'containers' child count and writing it: [rsp+0x90] = (r15 - [rsp+0x38]) >> 3 (0x143651bab..0x143651bb7), then rcx = [rsp+0x50] the stream and call [vt+0x48](stream, rsp+0x90, 8) at 0x143651bd5. [rsp+0x30] = the container (stored 0x14365106e), r12 = result. Raising [rsp+0x90] here changes the count the reader expects. The children about to be written are the SaveDataContainer pointers from [rsp+0x38] to r15 (the loop at 0x143651bf7 walks them).

verify.notes: V1113 sigcheck game.save_data_containers_count OK (1 hit, target 0x143651bbf); instruction boundary, no branch to it or into +1..+4 (function and image rel32/rel8 scans). 0x143651bab-0x143651bb7: rax=r15-[rsp+0x38]; sar 3; [rsp+0x90]=rax. Next: rcx=[rsp+0x50]; rax=[rcx]; rdx=rsp+0x90; r8d=8; call [rax+0x48], result to [r12]. Nothing writes [rsp+0x90] between the site and the call, so changing it changes the 8 bytes written. [rsp+0x30] is written once (0x14365106e, rcx unmodified since entry = arg1 container). r12=rdx at 0x143651052, reused as an iterator at 0x14365156b.., but restored from [rsp+0xf0] (stored at 0x143651516 while still arg2) at 0x14365173b and not written after, so r12 = result pointer at the site. [rsp+0x50]=[rsp+0xf8]=arg3 stream (0x143651729/0x143651731), [rsp+0x48]=k_Ne_BagCodecVtbl (codec {vt, stream}). Extra claim also confirmed: [rsp+0x38]..r15 is a heap array of child SaveDataContainer* built at 0x1436515e0-0x1436516f5 from each registered child-set node's +0x58 (filtered by groups [rsp+0x180] & (c+0xd0 ^ c+0xc8 | c+0xd8)); [rsp+0x38] and r15 are not written after 0x143651704; the loop at 0x143651bf7 walks rdi=[rsp+0x38]..r15, one entry per pointer, name from a stack property {0x145892430, child+0x70}, whose st64 writer reads the char* at string+0x10 = child+0x80, so a hook can read every name to be written. Count is (r15-[rsp+0x38])>>3 with sar (signed), i.e. child pointer count.
